**Origin**
Memorandum of March 2, 2022 from Rick West, Business Office, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (phone 248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013), to the Troy School District Board of Education. Recommendations come from Miller Johnson School Policy Services, the Board of Education Policy Committee and District Administration, broken down by Policy Manual section.

**Bylaws**
Policy 1000.02 Meeting of the Board of Education: quorum language modified and the Electronic Meetings and Remote Participation section removed, because Michigan Open Meetings Act revisions took effect January 1, 2022. A majority of serving members constitutes a quorum; a member not physically present may participate remotely if all attendees can hear and interact with that member, with 24 hours advance notice to the presiding chair. The deleted section had required one business day notice to the Board President, naming remote attendees in the minutes, and roll call voting.

**Students**
- 2000.01 Admission and Enrollment: children of non-resident employees may enroll tuition-free only if enrolling in the K-12 program; enrollment continues through graduation or certificate of completion, subject to long-term suspension or expulsion.
- 2000.02 Learning Environment: adds Child Find under IDEA and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, with notices naming Jessica Carrier as both Section 504 Coordinator and Director of Special Education, 248-823-5002, jcarrier@troy.k12.mi.us.
- 2000.06 Attendance and Truancy: expanded language referencing MCL 380.1561 and referral to Child Protective Services, police or prosecutor.
- 2000.06 Student Code of Conduct: additions for House Bills 5330-5332 covering criminal sexual conduct and cyberbullying committed off campus.
- 2000.06 Student Bullying: most granular language moves to the Administrative Regulation Manual, consistent with MCL 380.1310b.

**Curriculum and Instruction**
- 3000.01 Virtual Courses Allowance, added for the 2020-2021 school year, is recommended for removal.
- 3000.02 Parental Involvement: terminology discussion concluding the terms are interchangeable.
- 3000.09 Limited English Proficiency: rewritten around emergent multilingual students and the Michigan Department of Education Entrance and Exit Protocols.

**Personnel**
- 4000.02 Discrimination and Harassment and Nepotism, the latter expanding "relative" to in-laws, step- and half-relations and co-residents.
- 4000.05 Outside Activities and a new Illegal Conflicts of Interest provision citing MCL 380.1203 and MCL 15.321 et seq.

**Business**
- 5000.03 Purchasing rewritten; Federal Procurement Standards added referencing EDGAR and 2 CFR Part 200, delegated to the Assistant Superintendent for Business Services.
- 5000.05 Surplus Property broadened to facilities, real estate and other personal property.
- New 5000.11 Online Fundraising requires prior written Superintendent consent, naming DonorsChoose.org, Kickstarter.com, GoFundMe.com and CrowdRise.com.

**Facilities and Operations / General**
6000.02 Firearms and Other Weapons; new 6000.07 Private Transportation with IRS-rate mileage reimbursement; new 6000.09 Stormwater Discharge under the NPDES rules; 8000.07 Discrimination and Harassment naming Jordan Harris as Compliance Officer and Title IX Coordinator; and 8000.10 Animals on District Property.
2022_02_03022022_policy_update_recommend.verbose:
A memorandum dated March 2, 2022, sent from Rick West of the Troy School District Business Office at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (phone 248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013) to the Board of Education, outlines proposed updates to the District's Policy Manual as recommended by Miller Johnson School Policy Services, the Board of Education Policy Committee and District Administration, with the rationale for each change and revisions grouped by manual section. No recommended updates are offered for the Introduction section or for School and Community Relations.

BYLAWS. Policy 1000.02, Meeting of the Board of Education, is modified in its quorum provision and the Electronic Meetings and Remote Participation section is removed. The memorandum explains that the Michigan Open Meetings Act has undergone significant revision since the onset of the pandemic; after initially allowing broad latitude for online meetings and remote participation, those options were significantly scaled back in OMA revisions that took effect on January 1, 2022. Removal still permits remote participation in limited situations as provided in the OMA. The retained quorum language provides that, unless otherwise required or permitted by law, a majority of the serving members constitutes a quorum; a member not physically present at a duly held meeting where a quorum is already present may participate by telephone, teleconference, video conference or other electronic means so long as any attendee can hear and interact with that member, and the absent member must notify the presiding chair 24 hours in advance to participate remotely and may vote to the extent allowed by Michigan law. The deleted section required the Board Secretary to name each remotely attending member in the minutes, required the remote member to hear and be heard, required notice to the Board President at least one business day before the meeting so the public could be told how to contact the member, and required the Board President to ensure the public knew how any remote member voted, such as by requiring roll call voting.

STUDENTS. Policy 2000.01, Admission and Enrollment, revises the Children of Non-resident Employees provision so a child of a non-resident district employee may enroll without tuition only if enrolling in the K-12 program and not some other district offering; once enrolled the student may continue through graduation or receipt of a certificate of completion, without barring long-term suspension or expulsion for violating the Student Code of Conduct. Policy 2000.02, Learning Environment, adds Child Find language committing the district to identify and locate every student residing in the district who may be a student with a disability under the Individuals with Disabilities in Education Act and/or Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, regardless of whether they currently receive a public education, using advertising, posted notices, district publications including its website, and direct contact with parents. The notices must be easily understandable to a parent and must list the Section 504 Coordinator and Director of Special Education, both identified as Jessica Carrier, 248-823-5002, jcarrier@troy.k12.mi.us.

Policy 2000.06, Behavior, receives three sets of changes. Attendance and Truancy is expanded to require attendance every day school is in session except when excused, to direct the Superintendent to develop implementing regulations, and to allow referral to Child Protective Services or the appropriate police agency or prosecutor's office where a parent fails to comply with Michigan's compulsory school attendance law, MCL 380.1561. The Student Code of Conduct provision is amended because the Michigan Legislature recently passed House Bills 5330-5332, which require districts to expel, suspend and/or transfer students who commit criminal sexual conduct on school grounds or against another student at the same school; the code is stated to apply on school premises, en route to and from school, at district-related events and to off-campus behavior that substantially disrupts district activities or that the district is legally required to consider, such as criminal sexual conduct and cyberbullying. The Student Bullying policy is streamlined, with most granular language moved into the Administrative Regulation Manual in compliance with MCL 380.1310b while retaining the prohibition on bullying "at school" and on off-campus conduct likely to cause material or substantial disruption, protection against retaliation and false accusations, confidentiality for reporters, building principals as responsible school officials, annual Superintendent reporting to the Board of all verified incidents and consequences imposed, and definitions of "bullying," "at school" and "cyberbullying," including the off-premises use of a telecommunications access device or service provider owned or controlled by the district.

CURRICULUM AND INSTRUCTION. Policy 3000.01, Curriculum Development, is recommended for removal of the Virtual Courses Allowance added at the outset of the pandemic for the 2020-2021 school year under the Michigan Department of Education Pupil Accounting Manual. Policy 3000.02, Parental Involvement, is addressed only in commentary: some clients argue for "parental and family engagement," federal law since December 2015 uses "community and family engagement," prior federal law and the Revised School Code use "parental involvement," and the terms are treated as interchangeable. Policy 3000.09, Limited English Proficiency, is revised in its entirety, replacing "English language deficiency" language with a commitment to equitable opportunities for emergent multilingual students and English learners, identification under the Michigan Department of Education's Entrance Protocol for English Language Development Programs, and annual assessment measured against the MDE Exit Protocol.

PERSONNEL. Policy 4000.02, Employment Considerations, clarifies Discrimination and Harassment protections covering race, color, national origin, religion, sex, marital status, genetic information, disability, age or any other illegal grounds, cross-referencing Policy 8000.07. The Nepotism provision expands "related" and "relative" to father, mother, son, daughter, brother, sister, spouse, father-in-law, mother-in-law, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, son-in-law, daughter-in-law, step-father, step-mother, step-son, step-daughter, step- or half-brother, step- or half-sister, and any other persons residing at the same location. Policy 4000.05, Other Matters of Employment, adds to Outside Activities restrictions on paid tutoring of currently assigned students, tutoring during the school day or on district property, political campaigning on district premises or during work hours, use of district resources for political activity, and employee sales to students; and adds a new Illegal Conflicts of Interest provision citing MCL 380.1203 and Contracts of Public Servants with Public Entities, MCL 15.321 et seq., recommended after auditor feedback in other districts.

BUSINESS. Policy 5000.03, Purchasing, replaces the prior competitive-purchasing language with authority for the Superintendent to purchase or supervise purchases, to seek maximum value, to promulgate administrative regulations, to use competitive bidding when and as required by law, and to use competitive bidding or cooperative pricing otherwise at his or her discretion. A Federal Procurement Standards subsection is added acknowledging the Education Department General Administrative Regulations (EDGAR) and their gradual transfer to 2 CFR Part 200, the Federal Uniform Guidance, with responsibility delegated to the Assistant Superintendent for Business Services. Policy 5000.05, Surplus Property, is broadened from land and buildings to land, buildings, facilities and real estate, and from equipment and supplies to equipment, supplies and other personal property including identified surplus personal property. A new Policy 5000.11, Online Fundraising, bars any employee from creating, posting or sponsoring an online fundraiser using the District's name, logo or likeness without prior written Superintendent consent, and vests any property so obtained in the District rather than the employee, naming DonorsChoose.org, Kickstarter.com, GoFundMe.com and CrowdRise.com as examples.

FACILITIES AND OPERATIONS. Policy 6000.02, Safety and Security, adds language to Firearms and Other Weapons permitting law enforcement officers and security resource officers to carry firearms on school property, while employees and students who violate the policy face discipline including permanent expulsion or discharge and others may be banned from district premises and functions. Policy 6000.07, Transportation, adds a stand-alone Private Transportation policy allowing parents or guardians to request permission for a student to self-transport to and from a district site or program, prompted by a rise in lawsuits and insurance claims from students injured in privately owned vehicles driven by district employees, and authorizing employee travel reimbursement at the Internal Revenue Service rate. Policy 6000.09 adds Stormwater Discharge, responding to Clean Water Act amendments and the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System regulation of Non-Point Sources by the United States Environmental Protection Agency, and directing the Superintendent to promulgate administrative regulations.

GENERAL POLICIES. Policy 8000.07, Discrimination and Harassment, is aligned with the new Title IX regulations issued by the U.S. Department of Education and designates Jordan Harris, Compliance Officer and Title IX Coordinator, to investigate and resolve complaints and supervise implementation. Policy 8000.10, Animals on District Property, recognizes animals used in classroom presentations and housed on campus and the presence of service or therapy animals accompanying employees, students, parents, vendors and members of the public under federal and state law, applying to all animals including service animals, with administrative regulations to follow.

**Presentation**
Overview of Fiscal Year 2022-23 Oakland Schools Proposed Budgets, presented by Michelle Saunders on April 22, 2022, covering an enterprise-wide overview, the General Education Fund, the Special Education Fund, the Career Focused Education Fund and other funds.

**Budget timeline**
Nov 2021 develop budget assumptions; Jan 2022 first draft of FY23 budgets to OS Administration; Feb 2022 Oakland County Equalization presentation of taxable value estimates; March 2022 budgets submitted to LEAs; April 2022 meetings with OCSBO and LEA Board Designates; June 1, 2022 L-4028IC received from the County with the millage reduction fraction, rollback determined and LEA budget resolutions received; June 6, 2022 Truth in Budgeting Hearing and FY23 budget approved by the Board.

Expenditures: salary increase of 2% for all staff plus steps (approximately .98% union, 1.28% non-union), blended MPSERS rate of 28.26%, health care cap increase of 3.7%, and dental/vision reductions from a move to a premium-based program. Fund balance targets are 7.5% to 12.5% of expenditures for GEF and CFEF and 5% to 10% for SEF, net of LEA distributions.

An Oakland Schools slide deck titled Overview of Fiscal Year 2022-23 Oakland Schools Proposed Budgets, presented by Michelle Saunders on April 22, 2022, walks the Oakland County School Business Officials through the intermediate district's FY23 budget: an enterprise-wide overview, the General Education Fund, Special Education Fund, Career Focused Education Fund, other funds and budget timelines.

FUND DEFINITIONS. The General Education Fund is the district's general fund, supported by a property tax millage, state aid section 81 and other local revenue such as workshop revenue and technology licensing revenue. The Special Education Fund is supported primarily by a property tax millage and is the source of the PA-18 distribution to local districts. The Career Focused Education Fund is the vocational education fund, supported primarily by a property tax millage and state aid section 61, and supports the four Oakland Schools Technical Campuses (OSTC).

The fund balance protocol sets a target of 7.5% to 12.5% of expenditures for the General Education and Career Focused Education funds and 5% to 10% of expenditures net of LEA distributions for the Special Education Fund, considering known economic liabilities or designated reserves, the State of Michigan's economic environment and the financial condition of LEAs.
